skill.name: gsap-react
skill.description: Use GSAP in React and Next.js with scoped selectors, lifecycle cleanup, and browser-only animation setup.
skill.summary: Implement and review GSAP animations with React refs, useGSAP, and context cleanup.
skill.author: greensock

content.value_statement: React animations can affect the wrong elements or persist after a component unmounts. Use scoped GSAP selectors and React lifecycle cleanup to prevent these issues.
actual_capabilities: Register useGSAP and set up animations inside the hook.
Target a DOM node by ref or scope selectors to a component root.
Use dependencies and revertOnUpdate to rebuild animations when inputs change.
Revert a GSAP context during effect cleanup when useGSAP is unavailable.
Track animations created in event handlers with contextSafe and remove native listeners in cleanup.
Keep DOM animation setup out of Next.js server renders.
limitations: The useGSAP examples require the separate @gsap/react package.
DOM animations require a browser and cannot run during server rendering.
contextSafe does not remove event listeners or cancel scheduled callbacks.
The skill focuses on React integration, not detailed timeline or ScrollTrigger configuration.

use_cases.title: Animate repeated components independently
use_cases.description: Animate the children of each card list without selecting elements in other instances.

use_cases.title: Move animation setup out of server rendering
use_cases.description: Set up a Next.js section animation inside a client-side hook so it does not run during server rendering.

use_cases.title: Review animation cleanup
use_cases.description: Check whether animations and native event listeners are removed when a component unmounts.

prompt_templates.title: Animate one element
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to fade in a React panel on mount with useGSAP. Target the panel with a ref.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first GSAP animation in React.

prompt_templates.title: Scope a list animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate the items in this React list with a stagger. Scope the selectors to the list root so multiple instances can animate independently.
prompt_templates.scenario: A reusable component has repeated child selectors.

prompt_templates.title: Rebuild a tween when a prop changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this tween when endX changes. Set the hook dependencies and use revertOnUpdate to revert the previous animation before rebuilding it.
prompt_templates.scenario: An animation depends on a changing prop.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Next.js animation lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next.js component for animation calls during server render. Wrap click-triggered tween creation with contextSafe and remove any native listeners during cleanup.
prompt_templates.scenario: A Next.js component combines mount animations and user interactions.

output_examples.input: Fade in items for each list instance without affecting other lists.
output_examples.output: Each list has a root ref for its animation scope. Only that list's items fade in, and the hook reverts its animations when it unmounts.

output_examples.input: My button creates a new tween when clicked, but the component leaves a listener after unmount.
output_examples.output: The click handler is wrapped so the animation context tracks each tween. Cleanup removes the registered click listener.

output_examples.input: Set up an animation in Next.js without using the React integration package.
output_examples.output: The component creates its scoped animation context inside a browser-side React effect. The effect reverts that context during cleanup.

best_practices: Use a ref for a single target and a container scope for selector-based animations.
Use revertOnUpdate when input changes should replace the previous animation.
Wrap event-driven tween creation with contextSafe and remove native listeners in cleanup.
anti_patterns: Use an unscoped class selector in a component that can appear more than once.
Create DOM animations during server render.
Create animations in a regular effect without reverting or disposing of them during cleanup.

faq.question: Which packages do I need?
faq.answer: Install gsap for the animation library. Add @gsap/react to use the useGSAP hook.

faq.question: Can I use this with Next.js?
faq.answer: Yes. Set up DOM animations in a client component through useGSAP or useEffect, not during server rendering.

faq.question: What if I cannot use useGSAP?
faq.answer: Create a scoped GSAP context inside useEffect and return a cleanup function that reverts it.

faq.question: How do I keep selectors inside one component?
faq.answer: Pass the component root ref as the scope. Use direct refs when you need to target specific DOM nodes.

faq.question: When should I enable revertOnUpdate?
faq.answer: Enable it when a dependency change should revert the previous animations before the hook creates new ones.

faq.question: Does contextSafe remove native event listeners?
faq.answer: No. It tracks GSAP objects created by wrapped callbacks. Remove native listeners separately in cleanup.
